original_statement:
What must hold? State the invariant or expectation this concerns. `subchannel_close_value_preserving` in `ArmadaLean/Nitro/Liveness.lean` has a proof with no `sorry` in its own proof body.
What holds now? Describe the current, observed state. `subchannel_close_value_preserving`'s proof body is `sorry`. `scripts/check.sh --json subchannel_close_value_preserving` lists it in `sorry`.
How do you see it? Describe exactly how to observe this for yourself — the steps to reproduce, or how you would demo it. Run `scripts/check.sh --json subchannel_close_value_preserving` from the repo root and read the printed JSON object.
What constraints apply? State them in plain prose. The theorem statement does not change.
Where does this apply? (e.g. gateway route, mobile screen, CLI verb) ArmadaLean/Nitro/Liveness.lean, theorem subchannel_close_value_preserving
restatement: Complete the proof of the theorem subchannel_close_value_preserving in ArmadaLean/Nitro/Liveness.lean. Today the proof body is only the placeholder sorry, so no real proof exists yet. The worker must write a real proof term that satisfies three conditions at once. First, the proof body must contain no sorry literal. Second, the proof must actually compile: lake build must succeed on the whole repository with this proof in place. Third, the exact statement (the signature) of subchannel_close_value_preserving must stay the same as it is now; only the proof body may change. The repository already has a deterministic gate script for this, scripts/check.sh. Run it with scripts/check.sh --json subchannel_close_value_preserving from the repo root. It prints one JSON object to stdout. That object's theorem_in_sorry field reports whether the named theorem still carries sorry. Its build_ok field reports whether the build succeeded. Its signatures_ok field reports whether every approved theorem's statement text, including this one, still matches the frozen baseline. The proof is complete only when all three fields show success.
